segments.text: There are hundreds of voices in the kidney and transplant world. Hospitals have voices. Dialysis companies have voices. Drugmakers have voices. And the patients, the people who actually live this, are told that somebody speaks for them.

So we ask one question. Who pays for the voice? In a study of the hundred and four largest patient advocacy groups in America, eighty-three percent took money from drug, device, or biotech companies. Only one said plainly that it takes none.
segments.src: McCoy et al., New England Journal of Medicine, 2017

segments.text: In a single year, drugmakers gave a hundred and sixteen million dollars to five hundred ninety-four patient groups. Nobody was required to tell you.

stat.label: from drugmakers to 594 patient groups in one year

segments.text: We built the Cold Ischemia Foundation to be the exception. Not by promising to be good. By building it so that we cannot be bought.

We take no donations. No grants. No sponsorships. No money from drugmakers, dialysis companies, hospitals, or insurers. We charge a small, posted fee only when you ask us to do real work for you. And the basics are always free.

cards.head: Fees
cards.sub: only for work you ask for

segments.text: When nobody pays for your voice, nothing is off limits.

quote.text: When nobody pays for your voice, nothing is off limits.

segments.text: So we say what others cannot afford to say. We publish how every member of Congress has voted on kidney and transplant legislation. We publish every organ procurement organization in America, with its federal performance tier. And we send formal demands to Congress, to CMS, and to the OPTN board. Not asking permission. Demanding answers.

segments.text: We show our work. Every claim carries its source. Every essay tells you how we checked it, and what we could not verify. If we are wrong, we want to know.

cards.head: How we checked
cards.sub: and what we could not verify

segments.text: And we are built for the people this system forgets. The living donor who gives a kidney, and then has to fight to be made whole. The care partner who gives up a paycheck to keep someone alive. The patient who is told no, and never learns they could appeal.
Don't take our word for it. Check every number. Read their filings. Read ours. Then ask every organization the same question. Independent is not what you call yourself. It is what you can prove.

quote.text: Independent is not what you call yourself. It is what you can prove.

segments.text: We are the Cold Ischemia Foundation. We answer to one group of people. You.
